system.biography:
Background

Oliver Thrace has led the Hong Kong Chantry since Thomas Wyncham, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Inner Council's East Asian Representative, invited him to act as his primary agent. To all appearances he is the consummate @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} — governed by reason rather than passion, driven by loyalty to the clan and consumed by a thirst for magical knowledge, with a fearsome reputation as an implacable enemy of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}, Setites, and Assamites. In reality, Thrace lives a Masquerade within the Masquerade: after capturing a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} diabolist of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.rR0qLGz3CPcibovj]{Path of Evil Revelations} and stripping his mind of Dark Thaumaturgy, Thrace became a confirmed devil-worshipper, and his illicit trafficking with the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni} taught him Necromancy. He has quietly contacted both the Yama King Mikaboshi and the Yama Queen Tou Mu, hoping to play the two demons against each other — not realizing how transparent his scheming is to them.

Thrace's criminal underground holdings (prostitution, drugs, and other illicit trade) rival those of the 14K triads, fueling a bloody ongoing turf rivalry. Now that most Kindred have fled Hong Kong following the 1997 handover, Thrace is too stubborn to abandon his study of Kuei-jin philosophy and magic, forcing him into uncharacteristic restraint and subtlety.

Image

Tall, silver-haired, and well-muscled, Thrace has a jagged scar on his right cheek and wears an eyepatch over his right eye. He is never without a silver-tipped walking cane that doubles as a formidable melee weapon and bears diabolic ritual inscriptions (which the Kuei-jin believe make it a cursed artifact).

Roleplaying Hints

Ruthless in pursuit of material wealth and power over the spirit worlds. Maintains a facade of icy calm around clanmates (especially Wyncham) but is prone to frequent frenzies and secretly enjoys giving vent to his inner demons.

Haven

The Tremere Chantry, a small two-story building on Hollywood Road in Hong Kong's Western District, sandwiched between two brothels.
system.notes: Disciplines (as printed; convert to owned Discipline Items at Storyteller discretion): Auspex 6, Dominate 6, Fortitude 2, Necromancy 4, Obfuscate 4, Potence 4, Thaumaturgy 6 (Blood 5, Elemental Mastery 5, Lure of Flames 5, Movement of Mind 4, Spirit Thaumaturgy 5), Thaumaturgy (Dark) 3. Ratings above 5 capped for LARP play; restore book values for Storyteller-only scenes. Sire unlisted in source. Secretly Blood Bound his childe Wan Zhu in violation of clan law. Secret: contacts with Yama Kings Mikaboshi and Tou Mu.

system.description:
The Sielanic practitioner raises a spectral troop of mindless dead, called Drones, to act as defenders or to deliver warnings to her enemies. Though the tattered, ethereal images of long-dead warriors cannot fully materialize, they can hurl objects and frighten attackers. The ghosts return to their rest at the end of the night on which they are summoned.

System: This power costs two blood points and a Willpower roll (difficulty 7). The number of successes determines how many Drones the Cainite can summon.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Two: Usurpers

items.name: Thaumaturgy — 3 Advanced — Walk the Road of Shadows

system.description:
This power lets the vampire physically cross the barrier between the world of the living and the Underworld (Shadowlands) for a brief time, appearing to its denizens as a particularly solid wraith. She can interact freely with wraiths there, though she has no control over how they regard her, and any resulting combat causes real damage to both parties. Sielanic priests sometimes use this power to transport mortals into the Underworld as part of a shamanic initiation rite.

System: This power costs three blood points and two Willpower, and requires a Willpower roll (difficulty 8). A single success lets the Cainite penetrate the Shroud and enter the Underworld; three successes let her bring one other person along. She may remain until dawn forces her out, until she flees, or until driven out by the Underworld's residents.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Two: Usurpers
system.duration: Until dawn or the caster's choice

items.name: Thaumaturgy — 3 Advanced — Way of the Stone

system.description:
The vampire transforms himself into what resembles a stone dolmen, becoming immune to daylight and fire and capable of a very limited amount of movement — the source of legends of stones that walk at night. His features grow indistinct, taking on a semi-carved aspect, and the difficulty for all physical actions increases by two while movement drops to one-quarter normal.

System: The vampire allows three blood points' worth of his blood to drain onto a boulder, assuming its rough shape and consistency. Successes on a Willpower roll (difficulty 7) determine how long he may remain in stone form, from one turn (1 success) up to one month (6+ successes); he may abort the effect early if he wishes.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Two: Usurpers
system.prerequisites: Sielanic Thaumaturgy: Path of the World's Blood; must be attuned to the land

system.description: When issuing a Dominate command, spend a Blood Trait and decide how many future attempts to resist or recover memories you wish to crush, spending one Mental Trait per attempt (these Traits are unavailable the rest of the night, though Willpower expenditure restores them normally). If the subject tries to disobey or recover memories within that limit, agonizing pain incapacitates him for 10 minutes; the power fades once all guarded attempts have been used.
system.bloodCost: One Blood Trait, plus one Mental Trait per resisted attempt crushed
system.duration: Until the set number of resistance attempts are exhausted

system.description: Spend a Willpower Trait and win a normal Mental Challenge against a familiar target, regardless of distance, to establish mental contact as though eye contact had been made. Once contact is established, Dominate may be used on the subject normally; using this against another supernatural being costs an additional Willpower Trait.
system.bloodCost: One Willpower Trait (plus one more against supernaturals)
system.duration: As per the Dominate power used

system.description: Originally used to lead warrior-caste mystics on vision quests, this vizier technique lets a willing seer bring companions with him into the astral realms. All would-be participants must form an unbroken chain of physical contact with the character. Spend a Blood Trait for each "follower" you wish to bring along, up to a maximum of half your permanent Mental Traits (rounded down), then leave your body as per Psychic Projection. Each follower is treated as though she knows Psychic Projection regardless of her actual Auspex rating, using the leader's rolled successes. On the astral plane, followers must remain within roughly 100 feet of the leader, tethered to him and unable to break the connection. Any follower who loses physical contact with the leader instantly returns to her body and loses three Mental Traits, falling unconscious for the rest of the night if this reduces her to zero Mental Traits.
system.bloodCost: 1 Blood Trait per follower (max half permanent Mental Traits, rounded down)

system.description: After concentrating for a round on a familiar person, place, or object and spending a Willpower Trait, you win a Simple Test to perceive everything happening around that subject while remaining aware of your own surroundings. Other Auspex powers may be layered on to glean more, provided their own challenges are won. You must have known the subject at least one night, and must bid two extra Traits for challenges concerning your own physical surroundings while divided between two places.
system.duration: As long as concentration is maintained

items.name: Necromancy — 2 Intermediate — Call Forth the Host

system.description:
This power summons the spirit of the dead. The necromancer must know the name of the spirit she is attempting to summon and must possess some fragment of the deceased's corpse. The ceremony must be performed in complete silence but for the invocations themselves, lest the spirit flee in fear, and requires 15 minutes to complete. Vampires who achieved Golconda, or mortals who possessed True Faith in life, may not be summoned this way.

System: Win a Social Challenge (retest with Occult) against the spirit's Willpower to force its attendance; the degree of victory indicates the clarity of the spirit's communication. Each question posed to the spirit gives it another chance to break free, requiring the necromancer to repeat the challenge to maintain contact. A botch instead summons a malignant, lying spirit that convincingly impersonates the one sought.
system.source: Clanbook: Cappadocian, Chapter Three: Observations and Conclusions

system.description:
By holding the skull or brain of a recently deceased individual, the necromancer gains a mental image of the last thing to cross that individual's vision. This is an early, primitive fledgling use of the Giovanni family's necromantic art, taught in fragments to a handful of non-Giovanni Cappadocians before Necromancy fully matured as a Discipline.

System: The necromancer must hold either the brain or skull of the dead. Win a Mental Challenge (retest with Occult); the challenge is harder if the remains are more than a fortnight old. This power will not work if the subject had attained Golconda. The degree of victory determines the clarity of the vision, from a hazy sense of how the subject died to an infallible, picture-perfect vision of the cause of death, the killer, and the scene. A botch yields utterly false information.
system.source: Clanbook: Cappadocian, Chapter Three: Observations and Conclusions

vtmlarp.source: World of Darkness: Hong Kong (Hong Kong by Night), Chapter Four: The Spirits' Children
